subsystems.name: Light source and modulators
subsystems.role: generate and encode optical signals that represent input data and weights.

subsystems.name: Photonic matrix multiplier
subsystems.role: performs the core multiply-accumulate operation in the optical domain.

subsystems.name: Nonlinear activation
subsystems.role: applies the nonlinear function needed between neural network layers.

subsystems.name: Photodetection and readout
subsystems.role: converts the optical output back into electrical signals for further processing or output.

subsystems.name: Electronic control and memory
subsystems.role: programs the weights, controls the photonic circuit, and stores intermediate results.

subsystems.name: Packaging and thermal stabilization
subsystems.role: couples light into and out of the chip and keeps the photonic devices at a stable temperature.

buildSteps.title: Design the photonic circuit
buildSteps.detail: Use electronic-photonic design automation tools to lay out waveguides, interferometers, modulators and detectors on a photonic integrated circuit.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the chip
buildSteps.detail: Pattern the circuit on a silicon-on-insulator wafer using CMOS-compatible lithography and etching, often in a commercial foundry.

buildSteps.title: Integrate light sources
buildSteps.detail: Bond lasers to the chip (heterogeneous integration) or couple external lasers via fibers, since silicon does not emit light efficiently.

buildSteps.title: Package and couple fibers
buildSteps.detail: Attach fiber arrays to the chip edges or surface using grating couplers, and mount the chip on a package with electrical connections.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and program weights
buildSteps.detail: Tune phase shifters to set the interferometer mesh to the desired matrix, compensating for fabrication variations and thermal drift.

buildSteps.title: Test neural network inference
buildSteps.detail: Feed optical inputs through the mesh, read outputs with photodetectors, and compare against digital reference results for simple tasks.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with electronic host
buildSteps.detail: Connect the photonic accelerator to a conventional processor and memory to handle nonlinearities, data movement and overall control.

prerequisites.why: CMOS-compatible processes already make optical transceivers for data centers, providing a manufacturing base.
Heterogeneous integration of III-V lasers on silicon is demonstrated but not yet high-volume or low-cost.
Most optical nonlinearities are weak or require high power, making all-optical activation functions difficult.
Modulators in silicon photonics can encode data at tens of gigabits per second, fast enough for neural network inputs.
Tools for co-designing photonic and electronic circuits are emerging but not as mature as electronic EDA.

pathway.milestone: Lab demonstrations of small-scale optical matrix multiplication and simple neural networks
pathway.unlocks: proof that photonic circuits can perform core neural network operations with low latency.

pathway.milestone: Hybrid accelerators that combine photonic matrix multiplication with electronic nonlinearity for inference in data centers
pathway.unlocks: energy-efficient acceleration for specific AI workloads where optical multiply-accumulate shines.

pathway.milestone: Monolithic integration of lasers, nonlinear elements and control electronics on a single photonic chip
pathway.unlocks: scaling to larger networks and reducing packaging complexity and cost.

pathway.milestone: All-optical neural networks for ultra-low-latency and energy-efficient AI at the edge and in data centers
pathway.unlocks: new computing architectures that break the bandwidth and energy limits of electronics.
